title: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Motor Function and Fatigue in PD
official: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) to Improve Motor Function and Motor Fatigue in Parkinson's Patients
summary: The investigators hypothesize that multi-session anodal tDCS (atDCS) of the left primary motor cortex (M1) will induce long-lasting effects in improving motor function and reducing motor fatigue and fatigability in PD patients.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinical diagnosis of PD with at least two of the four diagnostic criteria for PD (tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability)
* Must be able to consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with dementia (MOCA \< 21)
* PD treatment using deep brain stimulation (DBS)
* Diagnosis of psychosis
* Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis
* Diagnosis of stroke
* Diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
* Diagnosis of congestive heart failure (CHF)
